about: Every number this video shows or says, with its source. From video/studio/research/runs/2026-10-28-trades-insights.md (bank lesson 1, 'Book the call, don't just answer it'); every page below re-read with WebFetch on Oct 28, 2026, evening (America/Chicago), and only what each page says is used.

servicetitan.title: The Profile of a Top Performer: Four Behaviors That Set the Top 10% of Contractors Apart
servicetitan.topDefinition: Top performers were defined as contractors in the 90th percentile of revenue within their trade and market segment.
servicetitan.quote: Top performers book 62% of their inbound lead calls. The rest average 39%.
servicetitan.gapQuote: That's a 23-point gap, and it sits at the very front of the funnel, where every dollar of marketing spend is on the line.
servicetitan.marketingQuote: If your booking rate is closer to 39% than 62%, the problem probably isn't your marketing.
servicetitan.firstMinuteQuote: It's often what happens in the first 60 seconds after the phone rings.
servicetitan.trades: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, garage door, water treatment, and other specialty trades
servicetitan.method: internal analysis of aggregated, anonymized data from participating ServiceTitan customers, trailing 12 months through January 2026; no sample size given
servicetitan.caveat: These metrics describe behaviors correlated with higher performance and do not imply that any specific product feature or practice caused the observed outcomes. Results reflect platform-wide patterns among participating ServiceTitan customers; individual results will vary.
servicetitan.scope: The page does not mention CSRs or define a lead call beyond 'inbound lead calls'. Said 'lead calls', shown 'lead calls'; the comparison group is 'the rest', said 'everyone else' (as lesson 5).

invoca.title: The Invoca Home Services Lead Conversion Benchmarks Report 2026
invoca.quote: 55% of home services businesses don't ask leads to buy or book the job
invoca.answeredQuote: Across home services, 52% of calls are answered by a person.
invoca.method: anonymized data from phone calls tracked and analyzed by the Invoca platform; averages across Invoca's customer base; nine home services sub-industries (carpeting, construction, doors and windows, home security, HVAC, lawn and trees, pest control, plumbing, restoration); time period and number of businesses not stated on the page
invoca.scope: Said 'home service businesses' and 'don't ask leads to buy or book the job', never 'never ask' or 'most shops'. The 52% answered figure is context for the caption only; not said in the voice.

servicetitanScripts.title: How HVAC Call Scripts Help Boost Booking Rates (With Examples)
servicetitanScripts.quote: Are mornings or afternoons better for you?
servicetitanScripts.where: Expired Memberships Script, step 6 (optional); said 'One of ServiceTitan's sample scripts asks it this way', never 'ServiceTitan's scripts always' or 'ServiceTitan recommends two times'

ask.source: OURS: advice, not a finding (the bank's call-close takeaway, reworded for a plumbing call; the job, the times and the days are examples)
ask.line1: Got it, water at the base of the heater.
ask.line2: We can take care of that.
ask.line3: I can get a tech there today at 2, or tomorrow at 9. Which works better?
ask.note: lines is the count of lines in the script itself; options is the count of time choices offered; neither is a finding

track.source: OURS: the weekly habit, not a finding
track.formula: booking rate = booked calls / lead calls, every Friday
